comparisonPages.coolify.articles.0.title: Focused app model & active Docker Swarm vs. SSH hosts
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.0.parag: CapRover keeps the mental model small: create an app, configure its domain, env vars, persistent directories, and replicas in one place, and let Docker Swarm manage rolling updates from your very first VPS. When you need more capacity, provision CapRover’s self-hosted private registry (or connect your own), republish existing builds, and join worker nodes for stateless replicas. Local volumes stay pinned to their node.

Coolify introduces a broader hierarchy—Servers, Projects, Environments, Shared Variables, and Resources—designed to manage independent hosts over SSH (including its own PostgreSQL, Redis, and real-time containers). Coolify’s experimental Docker Swarm support is officially deprecated and scheduled for removal in v5, so multi-server setups rely on standalone hosts plus an external load balancer.
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.1.title: Direct caprover deploy vs. Git-connected builds & rollbacks
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.1.parag: With CapRover, running caprover deploy from a local Git checkout packages your committed files and pushes them straight to your VPS—no GitHub App, OAuth integration, or external Git host required. You can also deploy from Git webhooks, prebuilt images, tar archives, or CI/CD app tokens. Coolify centers on Git-provider integrations (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea) with pull-request previews, and its CLI triggers builds from a configured source.

Both platforms support dashboard image rollbacks from retained local images or eligible registry tags. In CapRover, you pick a prior version in Deployment History; as on Coolify, rolling back an image does not restore earlier environment variables, database schemas, or persistent volume data.
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.2.title: Per-app NGINX templates & Docker escape hatches vs. Traefik/Caddy
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.2.parag: Most CapRover apps work out of the box with generated NGINX routing, automatic Let’s Encrypt HTTPS, gzip, and WebSockets enabled by default. When an app needs custom behavior—larger upload limits, security or CORS headers, IP allowlists, HTTP Basic Auth, caching, advanced redirects, or longer proxy timeouts—you edit the app’s full NGINX template directly, with automatic config validation and revert on syntax errors.

Coolify routes through Traefik or Caddy using generated labels and dynamic proxy files. For container runtime customization, CapRover also exposes Docker Engine’s native Service Update Override (JSON/YAML) for options like memory limits or read-only bind mounts, plus a JavaScript Pre-Deploy Function hook before service updates.
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.3.title: Compose imports or Git-managed stacks?
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.3.parag: CapRover has been publicly maintained since 2017 and modernized in v1.15–v1.16 with a redesigned Overview dashboard, guided Setup, 11 light/dark themes, live running-vs-desired instance health, task history, low-disk-space alerts, and a safer preflight --check installer. Its experimental Compose importer turns prebuilt image stacks into standard dashboard-managed apps and warns on unsupported fields like build or custom networks.

Coolify can keep a Compose file in Git as the deployment definition. Pick that workflow if each release should recreate a multi-service stack from the repository or if reviewers need a preview URL before changes reach production.
You want a lighter VPS starting point (documented 1 GiB RAM and 5 GiB disk minimum).
You want full per-app NGINX templates, Service Update Overrides, and Pre-Deploy Functions instead of proxy labels.
You want direct caprover deploy uploads from your terminal without mandatory Git-provider setup.
You want Docker Swarm as the standard runtime with built-in private registry provisioning.
You prefer a focused, single-admin Apache-2.0 platform with nine years of operational continuity.
comparisonPages.coolify.choice.competito: Your team uses Git-tracked Docker Compose files as the ongoing deployment definition.
You need one dashboard managing multiple independent SSH servers or Coolify Cloud.
Your team requires built-in team roles, pull-request preview deployments, or scheduled S3 database and volume backups.
comparisonPages.coolify.migrationDescrip: Convert Compose services into CapRover applications or validate prebuilt stacks with Apps → Docker Compose, map domains and environment variables, and migrate persistent data using your database or storage system’s own backup tools.

comparisonPages.dokploy.hero.title: App-first Swarm and NGINX vs. Compose-centric Traefik platform
comparisonPages.dokploy.hero.intro: Both platforms run Docker Swarm and offer a CLI. The difference is what you manage after deployment: an individual CapRover app, or a Dokploy application, Compose project or stack.
comparisonPages.dokploy.hero.verdict: Choose CapRover if you want to upload local code and roll back to a retained image on one VPS. Choose Dokploy if you want to keep services together in Compose or give team members different permissions.

comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.0.title: App-first Swarm workflow vs. Compose & Stack deployments
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.0.parag: CapRover organizes everything around individual apps: domains, HTTPS, env vars, persistent volumes, replicas, logs, and rollbacks live in four tabs per app. Its experimental Compose importer (Apps → Docker Compose) converts prebuilt image stacks into standard managed apps and warns in v1.16 when unsupported keys like build or custom networks are ignored.

Dokploy supports individual Applications too, but treats Projects, Environments, Docker Compose, and Docker Stack resources as first-class deployment units—a better fit when multi-service Compose YAML is your ongoing source of truth.
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.1.title: Direct CLI upload, built-in registry, and rollback prerequisites
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.1.parag: Both tools ship a CLI, but they solve different workflows. CapRover’s caprover deploy packages committed files from your local Git checkout and uploads them straight to your VPS without a Git-provider integration. Dokploy’s dokploy application deploy triggers a deployment from the source already configured in Dokploy.

Registry and rollback ergonomics also differ. On a single VPS, CapRover lets you roll back from Deployment History to any retained local image immediately—no external registry required—and when you scale to Swarm workers, CapRover can provision a self-hosted push registry in Cluster → Registries (port 996/tcp). Dokploy connects to external registries and requires a configured registry to enable manual rollback to specific deployment versions (in addition to Swarm’s automatic healthcheck rollback). In CapRover, image rollback leaves env vars and persistent data unchanged, and local volumes stay on their node.
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.2.title: Per-app NGINX templates & Docker overrides vs. Traefik & Swarm forms
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.2.parag: CapRover uses standard NGINX and exposes the full per-app template in HTTP Settings—ideal when you already know NGINX and need custom response headers, IP restrictions, basic auth, caching, redirects, larger upload limits, or WebSocket/proxy timeout tuning. Dokploy uses Traefik with domain rules, middlewares, and a Traefik File Editor.

For Docker Swarm customization, CapRover merges arbitrary JSON or YAML directly into Docker’s Service Update API (such as memory limits or read-only bind mounts) and adds a JavaScript Pre-Deploy Function hook. Dokploy exposes dedicated Swarm UI tabs for placement, update/rollback configs, healthchecks, file mounts, and raw byte/nanoCPU resource fields.
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.3.title: Maturity, v1.16 modernization, and complex team setups
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.3.parag: CapRover has been publicly developed since October 2017 under Apache-2.0. Recent v1.15–v1.16 releases modernized the experience with a redesigned Overview dashboard, guided Setup, 11 light/dark themes, live runtime health and task history, low-disk-space alerts, and a preflight --check installer—keeping the single-admin Swarm architecture intact.
Dokploy supports per-member permissions, remote build servers and scheduled S3 volume backups. These are practical reasons to choose it when several people share deployment responsibility.
Your VPS meets CapRover’s 1 GiB RAM and 5 GiB disk minimum.
You prefer full per-app NGINX templates and open-ended Docker Service Update Overrides over Traefik and Swarm forms.
You want single-VPS image rollbacks from Deployment History without configuring an external registry first.
You want CapRover to provision a private cluster registry from the dashboard.
You want direct local source uploads with caprover deploy and a pure Apache-2.0 project established since 2017.
comparisonPages.dokploy.choice.competito: Docker Compose or Docker Stack files are your primary deployment format.
Your team needs multi-user accounts, per-member permissions, or Enterprise SSO/audit logs.
You need separate remote deploy/build servers, built-in S3 volume backups, or Dokploy Cloud.

comparisonPages.dokku.metadata.title: CapRover vs Dokku: Open-Source Dashboard and CLI
comparisonPages.dokku.metadata.descripti: Compare CapRover and Dokku across simplicity, server requirements, open-source dashboards, deployment, Docker orchestration, NGINX, one-click apps and rollback.
comparisonPages.dokku.hero.title: Get a complete open-source dashboard without giving up the command line.
comparisonPages.dokku.hero.intro: CapRover makes the normal path visual and straightforward, while keeping CLI, API, NGINX and Docker controls available when needed. You do not have to choose between ease of use and infrastructure access.
comparisonPages.dokku.hero.verdict: Choose CapRover when dashboard operations, One-Click Apps, rollback and multi-node orchestration should be included in the open-source product. Consider Dokku when a CLI-first workflow, broad builder selection, cron and a composable plugin system are central requirements.
comparisonPages.dokku.resourceDescriptio: Both CapRover and Dokku document a 1 GB minimum with their default Docker-based runtimes. CapRover includes its web dashboard and Docker Swarm model at that published starting requirement.

comparisonPages.dokku.articles.0.title: The dashboard is the simple path
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.0.paragra: Domains, certificates, environment variables, persistent directories, replicas, logs and deployment history are visible and editable without assembling commands.
That makes routine operations approachable for every developer who can access the CapRover dashboard.
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.1.title: The command line is still there
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.1.paragra: Run caprover deploy from a local project, upload an archive, deploy an image or trigger a generic Git webhook. The dashboard itself uses CapRover's HTTP API.
CapRover adds a visual workflow without taking away automation or terminal-based deployment.
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.2.title: Simple does not mean limited
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.2.paragra: Most apps use the generated NGINX and Docker configuration unchanged. Advanced workloads can edit the complete per-app NGINX template and override native Docker service settings.
These controls stay out of the common path until an operator deliberately needs them.
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.3.title: The practical difference
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.3.paragra: Dokku's open-source core is intentionally CLI-first and highly composable through builders, commands and plugins. Dokku Pro adds its official web interface and API separately.
CapRover includes its visual operations workflow, One-Click catalog and Swarm management directly in the open-source platform.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.0: A full web dashboard should be included in the open-source platform.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.1: You want a simple visual workflow and direct local deployment together.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.2: You want deep NGINX and Docker controls available without making them the default workflow.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.3: Docker Swarm clustering and rollback should be managed through the same product.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.4: You rely on a one-click catalog of deployable applications and databases.
SSH commands and Git push should be the primary interface.
Buildpacks and a composable plugin system are essential.
You need built-in cron task definitions or global environment variables.
comparisonPages.dokku.migrationDescripti: Convert Dokku configuration into CapRover environment variables and application settings, add captain-definition files, map domains, and migrate datastore contents with the database's own backup and restore tools.
